# fortiappseccloud_waf_template_url_access

Configures URL access for one FortiAppSec Cloud WAF template using the static template endpoint `/waf/template/{template_id}/url_access`. This resource owns the template's module settings. To make an application inherit them, configure the matching app module resource with `template = true` and omit its `configs` block.

Declare only one `fortiappseccloud_waf_template_url_access` resource for a WAF template.

## Example Usage

```hcl
resource "fortiappseccloud_waf_template_url_access" "example" {
  template_id = fortiappseccloud_waf_template.example.template_id

  configs {
    status = true

    # Omit this ownership wrapper to preserve the complete remote rule_list.
    # Keep the wrapper but remove every item block to explicitly send [].
    rule_list {
      item {
        action   = "pass"
        name     = "allow-application-api"
        url      = "/api/application/"
        url_type = "string"
      }

      item {
        action   = "alert_deny"
        name     = "deny-admin-area"
        url      = "^/admin/(login|setup)$"
        url_type = "regex"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Argument Reference

- `template_id` (Required, Forces replacement) — WAF template ID.
- `configs` (Required) — Typed URL access configuration. Its attributes and ownership-wrapper blocks are identical to `fortiappseccloud_waf_url_access` when that app resource uses `template = false`.

## Import

Import using the template ID:

```shell
terraform import fortiappseccloud_waf_template_url_access.example TEMPLATE_ID
```

The first read after import hydrates all supported ownership wrappers.

## Destroy Behavior
Destroy performs a fresh GET, preserves the complete response, sets `template=false` and `configs.status=false`, sends the complete PUT, and verifies the normalized GET response before Terraform removes the resource from state.
